idiom_name: closure step list keyed by id + cursor loop (reduce for the pure form); @Sendable/async steps
implementation_notes: Swift closures make the itinerary a dictionary or array of async throws steps carried by an envelope value, applied with a while loop over a cursor, and Sequence.reduce folds a pure chain into a single function - so the classic Router/Step protocol hierarchy is replaced by closures, with value semantics (copy-on-write) making the envelope cheap to pass and mutate inside a loop. Combine's publisher chains are a deliberate cousin: operators compose at build time, not per message. Mark step closures @Sendable and keep them out of stored properties when they touch actors, and store step ids (not closures) the moment the slip has to be persisted or sent over the wire.
pitfalls: Closures are not Codable: a slip that must survive app termination or be sent to a server has to carry step ids and arguments.
An unstructured Task { } started inside a step outlives the envelope and can reorder progress; await the work inside the step or tie it to the caller's task tree.
Capturing self or a view/store in a step closure is the classic retain cycle and keeps the whole slip alive; capture only what the step needs.
Actor-isolated state mutated from a non-isolated step is a data race the compiler only catches if the closure is annotated @Sendable and isolation is modelled correctly.
